title: AGI Reactor proposed semantic and record contracts
status: Planned reference design; not an executable schema or ontology

definitions.definition: A service-owned entity with a stable ID, tenant scope, type, revision and attributed state. A file or database row is a storage representation of an object.
A principal is an authenticated identity. An agent is a persistent accountable identity with linked work and context; a worker process or model invocation executes on its behalf.
A service owns resources and exposes typed methods. A method defines inputs, outputs, errors, authority and recovery. Service identity survives implementation replacement.
Attributed communication between people and services. Chat is an IPC surface. A message may yield several tickets or edicts; receipt alone does not establish acceptance of work.
A durable obligation: intended outcome, acceptance criteria, state, zero or one assigned agent, and a result or explicit unresolved condition. Linked tickets express decomposition and dependencies.
One execution generation of a ticket, with bounded custody and a return point. A ticket may have many historical attempts and at most one current attempt.
A durable invocation identity bound to tenant, original caller, method, target and canonical argument digest. Custody may change; accepted intent cannot.
An edict is attributed, versioned direction. It may produce guidance, acceptance conditions or an authorization policy. Only its authorized promotion and activation make a policy enforceable.

A link is a typed, attributed relationship between objects. A binding is a link with operational applicability, such as a policy version applied to a typed scope. A link never creates authority by itself.
A skill is a versioned procedure assembled from guidance, templates and examples. It informs execution; it does not grant permission. These are content profiles, not separate kernel mechanisms.

The compositor resolves permitted sources into bounded working context with a source manifest, obligations, constraints, uncertainty and pending effects. A frame informs reasoning and confers no capability.

Evidence is an attributed observation or receipt with a declared scope. A projection is a derived view, index or summary of source records. Neither an inference nor a projection silently replaces its source.
A reaction binds a typed event to a governed method under explicit conditions; a routine adds a schedule. Both use normal admission, work and operation contracts.

An aegis is this design’s protected action boundary: identity, applicable policy, scoped authority and operation accountability. Its reference-monitor role must mediate access, resist bypass and be analyzable; the host and implementation must establish those properties.

records.semantic_fields: id, tenant_id, type_id, schema_version, owner_service_id, revision, provenance
records.invariants: Stable identity; owner controls writes. Tenant and ownership changes require explicit governed migration.

records.semantic_fields: id, relation_type, source_id, target_id, scope, revision, provenance
records.invariants: 0..many per object; endpoint types and relation-specific cardinalities are validated. Protected links are written only through their owning method.
The authenticated identity is distinct from a worker instance. Assignee, caller and reconciler remain separately attributable.

records.semantic_fields: principal_ref, scope, issuer, effective_interval, revision; allowance: dimensions, reserved, consumed
records.invariants: Grants require an authorized issuer and revocation checks. Admission reserves bounded resources atomically; concurrent reservations cannot exceed the allowance.

records.semantic_fields: service_id, method_id, contract_version, input_schema, output_schema, errors, recovery
records.invariants: A method binds a stable service role to its current implementation. Discovery does not grant invocation permission.
0..many source links to derived edicts and tickets. A transport envelope is not evidence that an obligation was accepted.

records.semantic_fields: outcome, acceptance, status, assignee_id?, result_refs, return_point
records.invariants: 0..1 assignee; 0..many attempts and dependency links. Accepted work is committed before acknowledgment.

records.semantic_fields: ticket_id, agent_id, generation, custody_expiry, recovery_epoch, status
records.invariants: Exactly 1 ticket per attempt; at most 1 current attempt per ticket. Current custody is checked at effect admission.

records.semantic_fields: ticket_id, logical_step, original_caller, method, target, argument_digest, outcome, custodian
records.invariants: Each record binds one immutable intent. Multiple operations per ticket are allowed; replay and replacement cannot bypass an unresolved logical step.

records.semantic_fields: source_refs, version, applicability; policy: rules, schema_ref, approval_refs, activation
records.invariants: 0..many derivation and scope bindings. Authoring, approval and activation remain attributable transitions; an edict is not automatically active policy.
Instances cite a definition version. Upgrading a definition must preserve existing instance interpretation or provide an explicit migration.

records.semantic_fields: source_ids_and_revisions, observed_at, scope, transformation; frame: compiler_version, required_context
records.invariants: 0..many inputs; provenance survives derivation. A receipt, hypothesis and verified result retain distinct evidence kinds.

information_layers.contents: Resource records, tickets, policy versions, grants, operations
information_layers.contract: The owning service is the write authority. Reads and mutations use its contract; the control/state service can host several owners as modules.

information_layers.contents: Catalog, graph lookup, search, embeddings, World State
information_layers.contract: Locate permitted objects by identity, type and relationship. Show source revision, observed time and coverage; rebuild projections from authoritative records.

information_layers.contents: Context manifest, required continuity, optional retrieved material
information_layers.contract: Resolve access before serialization. Preserve obligations, current attempt, pending operations, contradictions and return point. Missing required context is explicit.

information_layers.contents: Chat, object detail, diagrams, dashboards and agent frames
information_layers.contract: Render the same semantic records for each permitted consumer. A navigation category, frame or UI label does not become a separate source of truth.

information_layers.contents: Receipts, observations, comparisons, corrections, proposed skills
information_layers.contract: Link result to operation, ticket, input revisions and evaluation. Preserve contradiction and supersession; promote reusable changes through their owning workflow.

information_layers.contents: Sensitivity, retention, revocation, deletion and archival
information_layers.contract: Carry source restrictions into derived material. Invalidate affected caches and indexes; handle expired frames and retained audit obligations under an explicit policy.

ontology_primitives.meaning: A stable referent inside an explicit scope
ontology_primitives.expression: Object IDs and principal IDs; identity does not depend on a current process or display label.
Ticket, Agent, Service, Edict, Skill, Observation and Operation are domain profiles. Type definitions are themselves objects.

ontology_primitives.meaning: Typed endpoints, direction, cardinality and provenance
ontology_primitives.expression: assignedTo: Ticket → Agent [0..1]; dependsOn: Ticket → Ticket [0..many]; derivedFrom: Object → Object [0..many].

ontology_primitives.meaning: A governed request with a typed contract
ontology_primitives.expression: ticket.assign or report.send: input, output, error, authority and recovery semantics. Invocation is a message envelope; a durable effect has an Operation record.

ontology_primitives.meaning: An invariant or rule with a named enforcement point
ontology_primitives.expression: One current attempt; immutable operation intent; permitted policy scopes. Structural validation, authorization and lifecycle transitions have different checks.
